15.0.0.en: Christ likens Himself to the vine that bears us, who are its branches, the members of His body, and He also makes clear the responsibility of God the Father in caring for the branches of this vine. Every person in Christ who has no good works is a dead branch, which the Father takes away. But the person who is alive in Christ, the Father tends and prunes and purifies from sins by teaching and embrace, and by rebuke and trials at times, so that he may ripen further in the fruit of his virtues and grow in holiness.

15.1.0.en: The words here are to the disciples as good branches, and Christ makes clear the reason for their cleanness, which is their hearing and receiving His word.

15.1.1.en: This applies to all of us, for reading the Holy Bible, and hearing the word of God and acting on it, give a person purity, peace and understanding.

15.2.0.en: God's role in caring for the branches does not cancel the role of the branch (the person) in the salvation of his soul, for the person is required to bear fruit, and he has no means for that except abiding in Christ, the Vine. Is it conceivable for a branch cut off from the vine to grow?! Christ is the root of our growth and progress, and without Him we can do nothing. The abiding that Christ speaks of here reminds us of what He said before in (ch. 6:56): "He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him." That is, true abiding in Christ is through His Body and Blood.

15.3.0.en: But whoever makes light of the grace of God and does not abide in it, his end, his punishment when the just judgment of God is revealed, is:

15.3.1.en: (1) Being taken away, that is, having no part in Christ.

15.3.2.en: (2) Being gathered with the rest of the wicked like the gathering of firewood.

15.4.0.en: "If ye abide in me": through My Body and Blood, and all My commandments are fixed in your hearts and appear in your works, then your special gift is My immediate answer to everything you pray for. This is also what James the Apostle affirms, when he said: "The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much" (Jas 5:16). And a natural result of abiding in Christ, and of God's answering the requests of His children, is that the fruit of the branches increases in service and in the salvation of the souls of those far away, so that all the glory, praise and laud return to the Father. As for the pride of the fruitful branches, it is in the title that Christ gives them, "My disciples."

15.5.0.en: Christ found no comparison to describe the degree of His love for His disciples, and for all of us, stronger than the degree of the Father's love for the Son, a love that no man can describe. In the face of this boundless love, Christ requires us to abide in His love for us. The only means to that is keeping the commandments and obeying them, as He also obeyed the will of the Father, accomplishing redemption for all mankind (see ch. 15:10, 14; 14:15, 21-23).

15.6.0.en: "These things have I spoken unto you": that is, My talk about abiding in Me and keeping My commandments, so that you may have lasting joy. Just as Christ gave us a peace that the world does not understand, so everyone who strives to keep the commandment receives a divine joy that none of the joys of the world equals in its perfection and fullness.

15.7.0.en: Here the Lord Christ repeats what He mentioned in (ch. 13:34), that the level of love among His children should be on the pattern of His love for us. For Christ, in His love, humbled Himself and washed our feet, bore our sins and died for us on the wood of the Cross; indeed, He also forgave His enemies.

15.7.1.en: And none of us can offer an example of this love unless:

15.7.2.en: (1) He humbles himself with contrition before the One crucified for us.

15.7.3.en: (2) He continually contemplates God's love and forgiveness toward us, so that we can love and forgive others. (3) He keeps the commandments and acts on them.

15.8.0.en: In (ch. 13:16; 12:26) the Lord Christ gave His disciples the title "servants and slaves." And this is true, for before Christ, to whom be glory, there is no one who may be called "lord." But here, after the talk about abiding in His person and obeying His commandment, Christ moves His disciples from the state of slaves, who do not know their master's purposes, to the status of beloved ones and sons, who know their master's intent. And this is not a right of ours, but a proof of God's boundless love for His own.

15.9.0.en: Here the Lord Christ makes clear that, by His grace, He is the one who takes the initiative in the salvation of man by choosing him, and by appointing His disciples to bring forth lasting fruit.

15.9.1.en: As for the Father's answering all that we ask in the name of Christ, and in the face of the work of Christ's grace, there is a responsibility on all of us: to bring forth fruit at the level of striving for the virtues on the one hand, and the fruit of calling others to share in the love of Christ and faith in Him on the other.

15.10.0.en: The Lord Christ concludes this part of His discourse, affirming what He said before in vv. 9, 12 and 15, about the love between Him and His disciples, and among one another; for love is the protective shield for what He will speak of in the following verses.

15.11.0.en: The Lord Christ moves the disciples, and the Church after them, to what they are expected to find in the world of rejection and persecution.

15.11.1.en: And He gives all of us comfort and encouragement, which is that the world rejected Christ Himself. If we always remember this truth, it gives us patience and endurance, and we regard it as something natural.

15.11.2.en: And Christ makes clear the reason for the world's hatred of the children of God: they are different from it in their thoughts, opinions and spirituality, and therefore the people of the world, with their materialism and lusts, hate them; it is natural for darkness to hate the light that dispels it. And just as they did not receive Christ or His word, it is no wonder that the same is the case with the disciples and the Church.

15.12.0.en: Here Christ gives a new comfort, with which the disciples are to be comforted in the face of the persecution and rejection they would meet. This comfort is that He Himself is the reason for the world's rejection of them, for the world in its darkness did not know the Father, and therefore did not receive the Son. Christ here does not seek an excuse for the world, but condemns it for not believing in Him, especially after He had come ... and told ... and done wonders and miracles. So the sin of not believing in Christ remains; indeed, Christ adds also that the world's rejection of Him is its hatred of the Father Himself, for the honor of the Father and the Son is one and indivisible.

15.13.0.en: "They hated me without a cause": this verse came in its very words in (Ps 35:19), as though the Holy Spirit was foretelling, through David, the state and persecution of the Jews toward Christ without cause, so that Pilate the Roman declared that there was not a single reason for the death of Christ (ch. 18:38; see also Lk 23:4, 14, 22); rather, it was the malice of the rulers and priests that blinded them.

15.13.1.en: And those who today reject the call of Christ and His Church to them, are they not also considered haters of Christ without a cause?

15.14.0.en: Since the Lord's word to the disciples about the world's rejection of them was hard on them, Christ concludes His words by encouraging them with talk about the Holy Spirit, of whom He had spoken before (ch. 14:26; 7:39). For it is the Holy Spirit who will bear witness to Christ, through His disciples, before the whole world, by what they will say or the miracles they will do, whose source is the Holy Spirit. These are matters that gladden and strengthen the servants in every age, when they touch the power of the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church of God.

15.14.1.en: "I will send ... proceedeth": this shows the harmony and concord of the work of the three hypostases with one another. The word "I will send" highlights the divinity of Christ and His heavenly authority together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, and also highlights that the future sending of the Holy Spirit depends first on the redemption that Christ would accomplish on the wood of the Cross. The word "proceedeth" means continual coming forth from within without separation, as when we say: heat proceeds from fire, yet it has not left it ... So the Son, in His incarnation, did not leave the Father; and the Holy Spirit, in His procession, has left neither the Father nor the Son.

15.14.2.en: Chapter sixteen: Christ foretells His death to His disciples, the world's persecution of them, and the help of the Holy Spirit

16.0.s.en: (1) Christ foretells to His disciples His death and the persecution coming upon them

16.0.0.en: "These things have I spoken unto you": that is, all the preceding talk about the world's rejection and persecution of you. And the reason I have spoken to you is that your faith may not weaken, but that you may be strengthened by the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

16.1.0.en: Being put out of the synagogue is the severest penalty that can come upon a Jew, and it represents a moral disgrace; indeed, they would also be exposed to being killed. The motive of the Jews in that would be their mistaken zeal for God and the Law, as they did with Stephen (Acts 7:54-60). But the real reason for this persecution and killing is their rejection of Christ and the Father.

16.2.0.en: The same meaning as in the first verse. And He adds that He did not tell them from the beginning, for two reasons: first, their lack of moral readiness to hear this hard word.

16.2.1.en: Second, there was no need to refer to the work of the Holy Spirit the Comforter, so long as Christ was among them teaching them and strengthening them, and He was the source of their comfort.

16.3.0.en: "But now": that is, the events and dispensations of redemption began after the eating of the Passover, and Judas' going to the chief priests to agree on the arrest of Christ.

16.3.1.en: "I go my way to him that sent me": this means the ascension to the Father, passing through the Cross, then the Resurrection and its proclamation. "None of you asketh me": this is not a command from Christ, but a form of expressing wonder, as it came in the Greek: no one asked Him where He was going. The explanation of this is that grief filled the hearts of the disciples, because of Christ's talk about persecution and His separation from them, so they were occupied with what awaited them after Him rather than with the destiny of Christ!!!

16.3.2.en: I beseech You, my God ... we too often sink into our worries and grieve and are anxious, not looking to the dispensations of Your salvation and what You prepare for us ... Lift up our hearts and our eyes toward You, that our hearts may be strengthened and our resolve made firm, and that we may complete our lives with faith in Your promises.

16.4.s.en: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

16.4.0.en: Since the Lord Jesus felt the effect of His words on the disciples, and how they grieved, He wanted to move them to a place that carried comfort, and to lift them above grief. So He returned to reveal to them a secret of the dispensation and of the work of the Holy Spirit, making His departure a source of joy, carrying them over from sensory, bodily sight to heavenly sight. They might lose Him in visible sight, but Christ offers the Spirit, the Comforter who gives joy, as a better situation for the disciples and the Church, for the incarnation of the Son has a specific temporal mission that ends with the completion of redemption. But the Holy Spirit tends and cares for the preaching and the Church to the end of the age. Christ used here the attribute of Comforter as one of the attributes of the Holy Spirit, because the disciples were in the greatest need of comfort.

16.5.0.en: This verse is a summary before the detail: Christ presents the work of the Holy Spirit, then details it in the following three verses, which makes clear the importance of the sending of the Holy Spirit, and His varied work necessary for the salvation of mankind.

16.6.0.en: "He will reprove the world of sin": one of the works of the Holy Spirit is rebuke with the aim of pushing to repentance. However many the sins, the work of the Holy Spirit in the life of the children of God is to reveal the sin within them, then urge them to repent. The greatest sin is the sin of not believing in Christ, and without the Holy Spirit it is impossible to believe in Christ. See the prophecy of Zechariah: "And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him ..." (Zech 12:10); that is, had it not been for the descent of the Holy Spirit and His work on the day of Pentecost, many of the Jews would not have been "pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, what shall we do?" (Acts 2:37).

16.7.0.en: "Of righteousness": the direct and intended meaning here is that the Holy Spirit reproves the Jews concerning the Righteous One whom they rejected, who is Christ Himself. For when Christ came, who was their only hope of salvation and acquittal from death, they crucified Him!!! And the indirect meaning, from which all believers benefit, is that the Holy Spirit who works in them does not reprove them only for the sin they committed, but also reproves them for falling short in growing in the virtues, and in the righteousness with which they should be adorned and by which they should overcome their pride.

16.8.0.en: "Of judgment": that is, the Holy Spirit bears witness and condemns the world and its prince (Satan) for the trial of Christ. What appeared outwardly to be a victory for Satan and his helpers in getting rid of Christ became a judgment on Satan and the wicked world.

16.9.0.en: Because of the distress of soul the disciples were going through at that time, Christ did not tell them everything, but gave them as much as they could bear. But in the near future, after the descent of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, their eyes would be opened when they were filled with the Holy Spirit, and their knowledge of spiritual matters would increase, and the Holy Spirit would take over leading, guiding and completing the teaching. The Lord Christ points to the hypostatic nature of the Holy Spirit and His relation to the Father: He is the Spirit of God who takes from Him and tells the disciples the things to come, that is, everything that concerns the Kingdom of God.

16.10.0.en: "He shall glorify me": that is, showing the glory of the name of Christ in the Church and in the hearts of the disciples and all believers, after Christ hid His glory by His incarnation and His submission to and endurance of humiliation.

16.10.1.en: "He shall receive of mine": that is, even after My ascension and My bodily disappearance from you, He is the means of conveying to you My purpose, My thought, My teaching and My guidance.

16.11.0.en: "All things that the Father hath are mine": the word "all" here means complete equality between the Father and the Son. And because the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one essence, the Holy Spirit will take what Christ wants to convey to us, and He Himself will deliver it to His Church.

16.11.1.en: Here we note several functions that the Holy Spirit performs, which this chapter highlights:

16.11.5.en: (4) He conveys to the Church the purpose of the Father and the Son (v. 14).

16.12.0.en: That is, a reference to His death and burial, then seeing Him plainly at His Resurrection, then His ascension to the Father.

16.13.s.en: (3) The grief and joy of the disciples

16.13.0.en: It was hard for the disciples to understand what the Lord Christ said, so they whispered together, declaring that they did not understand His meaning. The Lord knew what perplexed them, and repeated what He had said before about their not seeing Him and then seeing Him, as a preparation for what He would declare and explain afterward.

16.14.0.en: "Ye shall weep and lament": that is, with the beginning of My sufferings, My crucifixion and My death; and "the world," that is, the Jews and their rulers, will rejoice, because they believe they have rid themselves of Christ forever. But be assured that after a little while, with the declaration of the Resurrection, your sorrows will turn into joys and glories that the world does not understand. Vv. 21-22: Christ gives a comparison that affirms what He said before, and uses, to bring it near, the example of the woman in labor, and the pains of her travail that she must pass through before these pains turn to joy at the coming of new life, for the mother's joy in her child makes her forget all the former pains. So will be the spiritual joy of the disciples, which is distinguished from all the temporary joys of the world in that no one can take it from the children of God. We have seen this very picture, not only in the life of the pure disciples, but in the life of all the martyrs, who offered themselves to death in a joy the world does not understand.

16.15.0.en: "In that day": that is, at the descent of the Holy Spirit, there will be no need for you to ask Me as you do now, for the knowledge that the Holy Spirit gives is complete knowledge, and it will be enough for you at that time to ask and request of the Father in My name, and the Holy Spirit will give you all you need.

16.16.0.en: All the pride of the Jewish man was that he would add intercession to his prayer with the names of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; but it became ours, in the glory of the New Covenant, to offer our prayers in the name of Christ Himself, as He taught us here. For this is the good pleasure of the Father, that all requests be offered through His Son who redeemed all mankind; and when asking in the name of Christ, there is an answer, and from it, full joy.

16.17.s.en: (4) The perfection of the disciples' faith

16.17.0.en: "I have spoken unto you in proverbs": I have been accustomed to speak with you in parables, to bring hard meanings near to your minds. But when the Holy Spirit comes and makes known to you the truths of the crucifixion, redemption and resurrection, there will be no need for parables, but the teaching of the Holy Spirit will be direct and understandable. And Christ regarded what the Holy Spirit will tell and declare to the disciples and the Church as the declaration of Christ Himself to them, because the Holy Spirit and Christ are one essence.

16.18.0.en: "At that day": that is, after the descent of the Holy Spirit and the birth of the Church, you will ask in My name as I told you (v. 23), and there will be a direct answer from the Father, because everyone who loved the Son and believed in Him entered, through the Son, into the presence of the Father Himself, and the Father gives him everything.

16.19.0.en: A completion of the preceding verse, and a full and concise theological explanation of the stage of the Incarnation and redemption, then the Resurrection, the Ascension and the sitting at the right hand of His Father.

16.20.0.en: In (vv. 17, 18) the disciples declared their perplexity about what Christ was speaking of. And after the explanation that Christ gave in (vv. 19-26), Christ summed up the theological truth in (v. 28) simply and in few words: that He came forth from the Father and became incarnate, then leaves the world and returns to the Father ... So the disciples expressed the clarity and plainness of the matter and their certainty of faith in all that Christ said, and also acknowledged their understanding that He came forth from the Father and came into the world.

16.21.0.en: "Do ye now believe?": the Lord Christ indicates that the faith of the disciples existed, but was so weak that it could not face the coming hours, which begin with His arrest and trial, then the events of the crucifixion. Therefore Christ prophesied to them what their state would be of fear, which would make them scatter, every man to his own, and leave Him to go through the winepress alone. Christ concludes His prophecy to them by saying that even if they leave Him, He is not alone, because the Father is with Him. And what Christ declared here is considered a translation of the Father's love for His incarnate Son on the one hand, and for all His children on the other.

16.21.1.en: My beloved brother ... if every form of persecution befalls us, and people leave us, and even our nearest ones neglect us, we have comfort, hope and faith in God, who never leaves us; and this faith is that from which all the holy martyr fathers drew their strength at the time of their torments.

16.22.0.en: "These things I have spoken unto you": this returns to the discourse in the previous three chapters, and the Lord Christ makes clear here the secret of His words in all that went before, which is that the world, which is in the grip of Satan, will be a source of pain, tribulation and persecution ... but I am the source of peace, so whatever you may meet, you must always have faith and confidence that "I have overcome the world," and I have given you also to overcome through Me ... Just as Christ crushed Satan on the Cross, and abolished the power of death and triumphed over it, so He also gave the disciples, and everyone who truly believes in His name, this victory over the world and the whole kingdom of darkness.

16.22.1.en: Chapter seventeen: Christ's intercessory prayer for us
